# The dependency-advisory gate, pip-audit, installed by
# .github/workflows/audit.yml — which then audits this file's tree along with
# the rest of the manifests.
#
# Why a manifest file when the install is one step in a workflow: Dependabot's
# pip ecosystem (the pip entry in .github/dependabot.yml, directory
# /.github/workflows) reads manifest files, never the pins inside a workflow
# `run:` block, so an inline `pip-audit==X` in audit.yml could only go stale
# unnoticed. Here the pin joins the manifests the weekly Dependabot pass
# already watches.
#
# Why deliberately NOT hash-pinned, unlike requirements.txt beside it
# (zizmor and PyYAML, installed with --require-hashes by actionlint.yml):
# pip-audit needs its own runtime dependencies, so hash-pinning it would pin
# its whole transitive tree — and the fresh transitives are exactly the
# subject this gate audits. Recorded trade-off: a transitive release can turn
# this gate red on an unchanged commit; that is the gate working, not a flake.
pip-audit==2.10.1
